metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened LibreOffice Calc, correctly identified B6='Nereida', switched to Chrome, attempted Google search for 'Nereida' but hit SSL certificate errors (NET::ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID). Spent remaining turns trying alternative approaches (DuckDuckGo, file manager, new tabs) but never successfully completed the search.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Calc cells, read cell values, switch between applications, switch Chrome tabs, type in URL bar and search bars, open new tabs
metadata.failure_analysis: Failed due to SSL certificate errors on google.com in the VM environment. The model correctly formed the search URL with the right query ('Nereida') but the page returned a privacy error instead of search results.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to navigating to a chrome:// internal page, which avoids SSL issues entirely. Tests the model's ability to switch to Chrome and navigate via the address bar.
metadata.explanation: Task requires opening Chrome's settings page by navigating to chrome://settings. Evaluator uses URL pattern matching on the accessibility tree to verify the active URL.

llm_judge_reasons: Instruction requires opening Chrome's settings page. Evaluator checks the active tab URL contains 'chrome://settings' via regex pattern matching, which correctly verifies the task.
Getter 'active_url_from_accessTree' extracts the active tab URL from the Chrome address bar in the accessibility tree, which is the right state to check.

Metric 'is_expected_url_pattern_match' correctly receives the rules dict (with 'expected' key containing pattern list) and uses re.search for pattern matching. The pattern 'chrome://settings' will match URLs like chrome://settings, chrome://settings/privacy, etc.
Expected value ['chrome://settings'] is semantically correct for verifying the settings page.

Minor concern: getter uses default goto_prefix='https://', which prepends 'https://' to the AT text, producing a malformed URL like 'https://chrome://settings'. However, since re.search finds the pattern as a substring, the match still succeeds.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider setting goto_prefix to empty string '' in the getter config for chrome:// URLs to avoid the malformed URL 'https://chrome://settings'. While it works due to re.search substring matching, it would be cleaner.
